title: Private Deployments: VPC & On-Prem Deployment Guide, Reference Architectures, Packaging, Day-2 Ops, Upgrade & Rollback, Customer Requirements Library
author: Arielle Nguyen
content:
Overview:

This document consolidates Redwood Inference's recommended deployment practices for Private Deployments (VPC-hosted and on-premise): a deployment checklist, reference architectures, on-prem packaging and installation guidance, day-2 operational runbooks, upgrade and rollback procedures, and a customer requirements library. It is intended for solutions engineers, platform operators, and customer infrastructure teams supporting private instances of the Redwood control plane and inference runtime.

Scope:
- Applies to Redwood Private (VPC and on-prem) control plane and inference runtime bundles.
- Covers initial deployment, day-2 operations, routine upgrades, and emergency rollback.
- Does not cover hosted API tenancy or Dedicated cloud-only managed pools.

Owner and Contacts:
- Document owner: eng-private-deployments (oncall: @eng-private)
- Primary author: Arielle Nguyen
- Suggested oncall escalation: Platform SRE team (pager: +1-555-0132)

Key Services and Components:
- private-control-plane: Kubernetes control-plane for private deployments (Helm chart: redwood/control-plane).
- deployment-agent: agent used for packaging and lifecycle ops (binary: redwood-private-ctl).
- inference-runtime: GPU-optimized runtime service (service name: redwood-runtime).
- telemetry-agent: metrics/log forwarding (prometheus-node-exporter + fluentd).
- kms-integration: KMS/HSM connector for customer-managed keys.

Prerequisites (customer side):
- Network: Dedicated VPC or on-prem VLAN with transit to customer management network.
- DNS: Domain record for control plane (e.g., cp.<customer>.example.com).
- KMS: Customer KMS key ARN (AWS) or HSM credentials for on-prem HSM.
- Storage: NFS/CSI-backed persistent volumes with >= 2TB for model cache; object store (S3/GCS/MinIO) for artifacts.
- Compute: GPU nodes (NVIDIA A100, H100 recommended) or validated CPU-only configs for small workloads.
- OS: Ubuntu 22.04 LTS / RHEL 9 (kernel modules: nv_peer_mem, nvidia).
- Kubernetes: v1.26- v1.30 validated (control plane and node kubelet versions must match validated matrix).

Quick checklist (high level):
1) Verify network & DNS (see Network & Security).
2) Provision KMS/HSM credentials and test key wrap/unwrap.
3) Provision storage (PV/PVC and object store).
4) Install redwood-private-ctl and run preflight checks.
5) Deploy control plane via Helm (canary first).
6) Validate runtime with smoke tests and latency/cost baselines.
7) Configure monitoring/alerting and backup jobs.
8) Document customer acceptance criteria and SLAs.

Reference Architectures (summary):
- Small (PoC): single Kubernetes cluster, 2x GPU nodes, single AZ, minimal HA. Use for evaluation only; no SLA.
- Production (VPC multi-AZ): separate management and inference clusters. Management (control-plane) in 2 AZs, inference nodes in dedicated GPU pools across 3 AZs. Autoscaling enabled with dedicated burst capacity.
- On-Prem High-Availability: three master nodes (VM or bare-metal), distributed GPU server pools, redundant NFS (gluster/CEPH), and on-prem load balancer (F5/HAProxy).

Architecture checklist table (recommended minimums):
| Component | Minimum | Recommended (Prod) | Notes |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| Control plane nodes | 2 vCPU, 8GB | 4 vCPU, 16GB | 2-3 replicas behind LB |
| Inference GPU nodes | - | 4x A100 / cluster | Use node labels for pooling |
| Model cache storage | 1TB | 2TB+ NFS/CSI | High IOPS for shard loading |
| Object store | S3-compatible | Multi-AZ S3 + Lifecycle | Artifact retention policy |
| KMS | - | Customer KMS/HSM | Envelope encryption required |

Network & Security requirements (detailed):
- Required outbound routes: control plane -> update.redwood.ai:443, metrics.redwood.ai:443 (for approved telemetry endpoints).
- Required inbound: port 443 for control plane LB, port 22 (optional) to jump host (restrict by CIDR).
- Inter-service ACLs: Utilize mTLS between control-plane components. Generate certs via deployment-agent or integrate with customer PKI.
- Security controls: RBAC (Kubernetes), OIDC integration for console access, and audit-logging exported to customer SIEM.
- Firewall rules example (AWS SG):
  - Allow TCP 443 from customer-admin CIDR to control-plane LB
  - Allow TCP 10250 (kubelet) from management subnet only

On-Prem packaging & installation:
- Packaging format: tarball (redwood-private-ctl-<version>-linux-amd64.tar.gz) and Helm charts (chart version pinned).
- Installer: redwood-private-ctl install --chart ./charts/control-plane --values ./values.customer.yaml
- Preflight: redwood-private-ctl preflight --kubeconfig /path/to/kubeconfig
- Example values snippet (values.customer.yaml):
  apiVersion: v1
  controlPlane:
    replicas: 3
    domain: cp.customer.example.com
    tls:
      provider: customer-pki
  runtime:
    gpuPool:
      nodeSelector: "gpu=true"
      resourceRequests:
        nvidia.com/gpu: 1

- Packaging notes: sign all artifacts (GPG), publish SHA256 checksums. For air-gapped installs provide offline bundle + documented steps for KMS integration with Physical HSM.

Installation procedure (step-by-step):
1) Run preflight checks and save report (owner: customer infra).
2) Upload Helm chart and set values.customer.yaml (include KMS/HSM config).
3) Install control plane in management cluster (helm install --namespace redwood cp ./charts/control-plane -f values.customer.yaml).
4) Wait for core pods to pass readiness probes (kubectl -n redwood get pods).
5) Install runtime in inference cluster(s) with GPU node selectors.
6) Run post-install smoke tests (provided by redwood-private-ctl).

Post-install verification (smoke tests):
- API health: curl -k https://cp.customer.example.com/health | jq .status == "ok"
- Model load: run sample generate call against sample model and assert latency < 200ms P50 for cached workloads.
- Telemetry: verify Prometheus scrape targets and FluentD forwarding to customer ELK.

Day-2 operations (runbook highlights):
- Monitoring & Alerting:
  - SLOs: control-plane availability 99.95% monthly, inference tail latency P99 < 1s for cached short prompts (customer-specific thresholds documented in acceptance).
  - Alerts: Node GPU memory pressure, pod restart rates > 5/hour, control-plane unavailable > 3m.
- Backup & Recovery:
  - Backup control-plane etcd daily (encrypted) and store in object store with 30-day retention.
  - Test restore quarterly in staging.
- Capacity planning:
  - Maintain 20% spare GPU capacity for burst. Monitor 7-day rolling utilization and forecast weekly.
- Common operational tasks:
  - Clear model cache: redwood-private-ctl cache flush --namespace inference
  - Rotate TLS certs: redwood-private-ctl cert rotate --component control-plane --expiry 90d
  - KMS key rotation coordination with customer KMS owner

Upgrade and Rollback procedures (recommended practice):
- Strategy: Canary rollout with progressive traffic shift (10% -> 50% -> 100%). Always run upgrade in staging first.
- Pre-upgrade: Create snapshot of etcd, export configuration, and create a rollback tag for Helm charts.
- Upgrade steps (control plane):
  1) helm upgrade --install cp ./charts/control-plane -f values.customer.yaml --atomic --timeout 15m
  2) Monitor health checks and SLOs for 10-15 minutes on canary slice.
  3) If canary passes, continue progressive rollout across remaining nodes.
- Rollback steps (if failure detected):
  1) helm rollback cp <previous-release> --kube-namespace redwood
  2) Restore etcd snapshot if helm rollback does not restore state: redwood-private-ctl etcd restore --snapshot <path>
  3) Run smoke tests and validate API and model loading.
- Automated rollback triggers:
  - >= 3 control-plane restarts in 10m or SLO breach detected during canary window.

Validation and acceptance tests (automated):
- Test suite includes: health check, model sampling, throughput test (tokens/sec), latency distributions (P50/P95/P99), and security checks (s3 write/read, kms encrypt/decrypt).
- Post-upgrade acceptance gates must be recorded and signed off by customer SRE and Redwood Solutions Engineer.

Customer Requirements Library (high-level entries):
- Networking: Must provide CIDR for management access, allowed egress to update endpoints, and private peering details.
- Compliance: Provide list of regulatory requirements (e.g., HIPAA, SOC2) and required audit log retention windows.
- Hardware: Provide GPU model, firmware versions, BIOS settings, and out-of-band management (iDRAC/iLO) access for hardware support.
- KMS: Provide key rotation policy, key IDs, and HSM vendor details when applicable.
- Backup: Acceptable RTO/RPO values and designated object store bucket for snapshots.

Customer requirements quick table (example):
- Minimum network throughput: 1Gbps per GPU host
- TLS termination: Customer LB or Redwood-managed cert? (customer LB recommended for on-prem)
- Audit log retention: 90 days (standard) or customer-specified

Operational Playbooks (links to short procedures):
- Incident: Control plane down -> Runbook: escalate to Platform SRE -> Activate incident bridge -> Run minimal restore steps.
- Security: Suspected key compromise -> Quarantine keys, rotate KMS, and initiate forensics.
- Capacity event: Scale up GPU pool using autoscaling policy and notify account team.

Appendices:
A. Example Helm commands and common flags:
- helm install cp ./charts/control-plane -n redwood -f values.customer.yaml --wait --timeout 10m
- helm upgrade cp ./charts/control-plane -f values.customer.yaml --reuse-values

B. Example verification script (bash snippet):
  #!/bin/bash
  set -e
  HEALTH=$(curl -s -k https://cp.customer.example.com/health | jq -r .status)
  if [[ "$HEALTH" != "ok" ]]; then
    echo "Control plane unhealthy"
    exit 1
  fi
  echo "Control plane healthy"

C. Versioning & compatibility matrix (short):
- redwood-private-ctl: v1.20+ required for Kubernetes 1.28+
- Charts: control-plane v2.x compatible with runtime v3.x (check release notes for exact mapping)

Document maintenance:
- Review cadence: Quarterly or aligned with major release windows.
- Update owner: eng-private-deployments. Add reviewer notes for major schema or API changes.
